scope: 59 existing everyday topics, adding exact Swahili contexts in twenty directions. No reserved dialogue turns were used.

decisions.lexical_scope: Explicit brackets identify one lexical focus. Person, tense, ownership, case particles, articles and negation stay outside it. Existing ten-language strings retain their prior article corrections and readable Latin forms.
decisions.locatives: Niko ofisini and Niko nyumbani retain the attested locative ni outside the noun focus ofisi or nyumba. These exact contexts do not authorize arbitrary suffix stripping, a general stemmer or interpolation of other people's grammar.
decisions.compounds: Airport, breakfast, lunch, dinner, weekend, email and weather use their complete conventional noun phrases. Their internal Swahili agreement is part of the lexical unit. Their external tense, modifier and possession are preserved.
decisions.bound_senses: Simu inaita identifies a ringing telephone; Nilipiga picha identifies taking a photograph; Kazi is a job only in Ninatafuta kazi; Mazungumzo is conversation within the complete telephone-call context. No bare-word generalization is approved.
decisions.omissions: Birthday and homework sentences whose possession interrupts the Swahili noun phrase are omitted. Chinese source question/problem ambiguity and Arabic family ownership exclusions are preserved. No broad or discontinuous focus is introduced to increase counts.
decisions.review: The author inspected the 59 Swahili references and lexical scopes against the existing topic meanings. This is content-bound author assessment, not independent linguistic review or measurement of unseen conversation accuracy.

limitations: Exact contexts only; additional references do not establish majority conversation coverage.
Regional phrasing and machine translation synonyms may prevent otherwise useful matches.
Native execution and original-text preservation must be qualified separately.
